title: Service Dependability: Roles and Communication Playbook
content:
Purpose:
This working playbook defines cross-functional roles, primary communication channels, and an escalation model to operationalize SLO commitments for customer-facing model serving lanes. It’s intended as the minimal runnable agreement between Feature Teams, Platform, Dedicated Ops, and SRE until a formal runbook repo and automation are in place.

Scope and assumptions:
- Scope: customer-facing text-generation API (hosted + dedicated pools) and critical infra components (routing, cache, KV-store backups).
- Assumes teams maintain their feature-level runbooks; this doc focuses on cross-team interlocks, handoffs, and cadence.
- Not a technical incident playbook for deep debugging — those live in the runbook repo, referenced below.

Key outcomes we want in 90 days:
- Clear role matrix and one-page escalation flows per service family.
- Agreed capacity-commitment ledger for Dedicated pools for Q1 usage spikes.
- Communication templates (postmortem skeleton, status update cadence, oncall handoff notes).
- Two cross-team tabletop exercises validating SLO cutovers and fallback policies.

Primary stakeholders (who signs up):
- Service Owners (Feature teams): product + owning eng leads — maintain SLI definitions and alert thresholds.
- Platform / Serving Runtime: responsible for routing policies, model fallback, and capacity APIs.
- SRE (this doc owner): availability guardrails, incident coordination, and blameless postmortem lead.
- Dedicated Ops: capacity commitments, reserved pool config, billing/quota contact.
- Support & CS: customer-facing comms and severity classification.

Roles & responsibilities (one-liners):
- Incident Commander (IC): drives the immediate response, coordinates cross-team actions, and owns status updates until the bridge is handed over.
- Triage Owner: validates alerts, maps to SLIs, and determines escalation (IC or watch).
- Service SME: feature-level expert for debugging and mitigations.
- Platform SME: implements capacity or routing changes (e.g., emergency reroute to older model family).
- Customer Liaison (CS): drafts external comms and coordinates with legal/PR if needed.
- Reliability Steward (SRE): post-incident analysis and SLO remediation plan.

Communication channels (primary + fallback):
- Primary: #ops-availability Slack channel (thread per incident), documented bridge link and incident doc in the runbook repo.
- Fallback: Pager escalation to IC (voice bridge template in Confluence).
- Async: Status doc (Google doc) updated every 20 minutes for Sev1 until recovery.
- External: CS-owned status.redwood.ai incident post if customer-visible.

Escalation flow (summary):
1) Alert fires -> Triage Owner evaluates within 3 minutes.
2) If confirmed and severity >= S2 (user impact on >10% requests) -> IC paged.
3) IC opens bridge, notifies Platform SME and Service SME, posts initial status in Slack and status doc.
4) If capacity shortage suspected -> Dedicated Ops notified for immediate pool adjustments/fallback.
5) IC decides whether to route to lower-cost model variant or enable degraded mode; Platform SME executes.
6) After stabilization -> IC hands over to Reliability Steward for postmortem.

Oncall handshake and handoff template (to embed in runbooks):
- Handoff time window: 5 minutes to acknowledge, 15 minutes to share top-3 unknowns and current mitigations.
- Handoff fields: incident id, trigger, timeline (first alert -> actions taken), current mitigation, required follow-ups.

Capacity commitment ledger (working table, sample rows):
- Feature-team A: reserved 4 A100-equivalent slots on weekdays 08:00-20:00 PST for peak inference pipelines.
- Feature-team B: burstable up to 3 extra slots for scheduled campaigns (requires 24h notice to Dedicated Ops).
- Platform: maintains 10% emergency buffer across regions; auto-eviction policy documented.
(This is a lightweight ledger now — will move into a shared spreadsheet and a short API with Dedicated Ops).

SLO acceptance and release gates (for new model / config rollouts):
- Pre-cutover checklist: baseline latency & error SLIs, traffic shadowing for 24h with perf monitor, fallback model registered.
- Cutover gate: 1h live canary at 1% traffic, measure token-latency P95, availability, and model-output-quality (sample prompts).
- Abort conditions: P95 latency > 1.5x baseline OR error-rate delta > 0.5% absolute OR functional regression on evaluation prompts.

Tabletop exercise plan (90-day timeline):
- Week 2: SLO ownership tabletop (45 minutes) — validate roles and Slack/bridge behavior.
- Week 6: Capacity exhaustion drill — simulate pool exhaustion and validate fallback path.
- Week 10: Customer-visible outage run — include CS and legal for external comms practice.
- Deliverable post-exercise: short action list and owners, to be tracked in JIRA-RELI-1123.

Runbook templates and artifacts (links + brief):
- Incident overview doc template (what happened, timeline, mitigation actions, customer impact).
- Quick mitigations checklist (reroute, model-variant enable, scale pool).
- Postmortem template with corrective actions and SLO remediation plan.

Open questions & decisions required (high priority):
- How strict is the emergency buffer? Platform proposes dynamic buffer down to 5% if utilization > 85% for 24h (Dedicated Ops must sign off).
- SLA language alignment: do we map SLOs to billing credits or only internal guardrails? Legal/finance input needed.
- Can we automate the capacity-commitment ledger into Dedicated Ops APIs within Q1? Platform + Infra feasibility follow-up.

Risks and mitigations (short list):
- Risk: unclear owner during blended incidents spanning multiple services -> Mitigation: IC role must be assigned by first acknowledged responder; SRE rotates a secondary IC until service owner joins.
- Risk: noisy alerts obscure real incidents -> Mitigation: adjust thresholds for model-serving SLIs and add signal quality pipeline.
- Risk: rollback causes customer-facing regressions -> Mitigation: shadowing and progressive traffic ramp with canary gates; maintain older model variants for quick fallback.

Next actions (owners & short deadlines):
- Maya (SRE): publish a 1-page TL;DR and the Slack templates by 2024-11-22.
- Platform (Ethan): propose capacity-API spec for ledger by 2024-12-05.
- Dedicated Ops (Priya): confirm emergency buffer policy and eviction rules by 2024-12-12.
- CS (Sophie): draft external incident template and severity mapping by 2024-12-01.

Notes to reviewers (quick):
- This is intentionally pragmatic: keep it lightweight and actionable. Add concrete owners and push technical runbooks to the runbook repo.
- Please comment inline with alternatives rather than rewriting sections; we’ll schedule a 30-minute sync to converge on approvals.

Relevant links and references:
- Confluence: /pages/viewpage.action?pageId=3456 (Service contracts and SLO glossary)
- Runbook repo: github.com/redwood-inference/ops-runbooks (incident templates + automation hooks)
- Jira Epic: JIRA-RELI-1123 (Cross-team reliability sprint)

Appendix (cheat-sheet for IC):
- First 5 minutes: confirm triage, page IC, open bridge, post initial status.
- 5–30 minutes: gather platform + service SMEs, implement short-term mitigations.
- 30–90 minutes: stabilize, communicate cadence, decide whether to escalate to exec/CS.
- Post incident: handover to Reliability Steward for postmortem and SLO remediation plan.

Unresolved (parking lot):
- Persistent automation for alert-to-incident mapping (integrate with telemetry service).
- Standardized severity definitions across CS and SRE (current overlaps cause mismatch).

End of working draft.
summary: Working playbook (draft) that defines cross-team communication, escalation flow, capacity commitments, tabletop timelines, and action owners to operationalize SLOs for model-serving services.
